attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The actual endpoint incidence table B_v and uniform tail interval are still missing at proof level; the derivation gives the sharp scalar certificate but not the numerical or analytic endpoint-box bounds.
steps: Conceptual pressure attacked: the branch must decide the post-H,K endpoint R/kappa_4 term, not restate OS positivity or the earlier hairpin threshold.
Start with the fixed three-hairpin null channel after the valid Schur-Feshbach correction; denote its remaining scalar by S_end=M_G+R_end with M_G>0.
Use heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulation and write R_end as a sum of endpoint-box connected fourth Wilson flux cumulants plus a corner tail.
Connected log cumulants remove Wick-square Gram pieces; the null incidence identity cancels the straight-segment C_A f f commutator contact.
The local compact-group fourth cumulant has sign kappa_4^{sing}=-beta_v with beta_v>=0 in the small heat-kernel endpoint box.
Contracting with the null weights produces D_v=2G12(v)-4G13(v)-4G23(v); hence negative kappa_4 is harmful only where D_v>0.
Separating D_v into positive and negative parts gives a valid clipped bound: only sum beta_v[D_v]_+ competes against M_G, while beta_v[-D_v]_+ is protective.

Hard gate: produce certified intervals for beta_v, D_v, and T_a. Success promotes this finite Wilson block through the post-H,K handoff; failure by a negative interval gives an explicit same-theory OS falsifier.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a regulated finite-block reduction. It does not prove continuum Yang-Mills existence, mass gap, or OS positivity for the full Wilson algebra until the endpoint source intervals, tail bounds, and cutoff-removal stability are certified.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Post-H,K endpoint-box clipping for reflected Wilson hairpins

assumptions: Model: four-dimensional Euclidean SU(N) Yang-Mills approximated by heat-kernel plaquette sheets before cutoff removal.
Regime: endpoint boxes are smaller than the collar scale but larger than the plaquette cutoff, so local heat-kernel cumulant expansion is uniform.
Uniformity: the eighth-source-derivative bound controlling endpoint stencils is summable over endpoint boxes.
Cancellation: connected logarithms remove Wick-square disconnected terms, and the null incidence identity removes straight C_A f f contacts on shared straight segments.
Same-theory condition: Wilson loops are not reweighted at the reflection plane and the endpoint source derivatives are evaluated in the locked gauge-invariant algebra.
definitions: source object: regulated SU(N) heat-kernel plaquette-sheet Wilson three-hairpin collar block with endpoint boxes v, singlet fourth flux cumulants, and fixed color normalization T_F/N.
target object: the post-H,K Schur-Feshbach null-channel scalar whose positivity decides same-theory OS positivity for this finite Wilson block.
controlled interface: contraction of the connected endpoint Wilson cumulant with the Feshbach null vector a=(1,1,-2), represented by endpoint overlap entries G_ij(v).

same-theory condition: the same heat-kernel Wilson observable algebra, loop renormalization, endpoint partition functions, and color conventions are used for the collar limit and the intended quotient matrix; no boundary counterterm is inserted.
M_G is the positive Gaussian Schur-Feshbach margin already left after PHP and the corrected second-order form.
beta_v=-kappa_{4,v}^{sing} is the positive magnitude of the local compact-group fourth cumulant in endpoint box v.
T_a is the residual endpoint/corner tail after removing Wick-square Gram terms and the straight f f contact.

equations.label: endpoint scalar decomposition
equations.latex: \mathcal S_{\rm end}=M_G+\mathcal R_{\rm end},\qquad \mathcal R_{\rm end}=-\alpha_a\sum_{v}\beta_v D_v+\mathcal T_a,\quad \alpha_a={g_a^4\over4}\left({T_F\over N}\right)^2
equations.valid_when: Applies after heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regularization, after H,K are fixed, and after Wick-square plus straight-contact cancellations are valid.

equations.label: incidence polarization
equations.valid_when: Valid when G12(v) is nonzero and endpoint overlaps are computed from the same null-channel Wilson incidence table.

equations.label: clipped promotion bound
equations.valid_when: Requires beta_v nonnegative for the compact-group endpoint cumulant and a certified absolute bound on all endpoint and corner tails.

equations.label: interval falsifier test
equations.valid_when: Valid for interval arithmetic whose lower and upper bounds enclose the regulated endpoint source derivatives before continuum extrapolation.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Demote the lemma if beta_v is not sign-certified, if endpoint tails are nonlocal at the same order, or if the incidence table changes under cutoff removal.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This is the contribution-making post-H,K reduction: it turns the remaining R/kappa_4 endpoint term into a signed finite endpoint dominance test rather than a symbolic R parameter.
candidate_lemmas.statement: After the three-hairpin H,K gate is fixed, the remaining connected boundary-OPE polarization is controlled by a clipped endpoint half-dominance quantity. In heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulation, negative compact-group fourth cumulants are dangerous only at endpoint boxes with D_v=2G12(v)-4G13(v)-4G23(v)>0, equivalently eta_v=(G13+G23)/G12<1/2. Thus equal or symmetric endpoint boxes promote the block; only certified 12-dominance or a negative tail can be a falsifier.

assumptions: The endpoint source path s -> exp(sB_v) remains inside the heat-kernel chart for |s|<=3h.
The eighth derivative of log Z_v along B_v is bounded by M_{8,v} uniformly in the cutoff window.
The regulator uses the same lattice orientation and color trace convention in all three pair entries.
The finite difference is used only as a certified endpoint-box estimate, not as a continuum proof by itself.
definitions: source object: endpoint-box heat-kernel partition function Z_v(s)=Z_v(exp(sB_v)) with B_v the null-channel Wilson flux source.
target object: interval bounds for beta_v D_v entering the scalar Schur-Feshbach endpoint test.
controlled interface: seven-point fourth-difference extraction of d_s^4 log Z_v(0), combined with the endpoint incidence coefficient D_v.
same-theory condition: the source B_v is built from the same plaquette-sheet Wilson insertions used in the collar Schwinger forms.

equations.label: seven point endpoint stencil
equations.valid_when: Applies when ell_v(s)=log Z_v(s) is C^8 on the full seven-point source interval.

equations.label: stencil error
equations.valid_when: Requires the eighth source derivative bound along the endpoint Wilson source direction for every point in the stencil.

equations.label: endpoint cumulant interval
equations.valid_when: Valid when D_v is the already computed same-theory endpoint incidence scalar and no extra boundary source is introduced.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Fails if the endpoint source chart is too small for a symmetric stencil or if M_8 grows faster than the endpoint localization gain.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Provides the finite regulator computation needed for the clipped promotion or falsifier inequality.
candidate_lemmas.statement: The dangerous clipped quantity can be certified without diagonalizing an endpoint cumulant matrix: for each endpoint box, a one-dimensional source derivative along the null-channel endpoint source gives beta_v D_v with a controlled finite-difference remainder.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine if beta_v sign, straight-contact cancellation, or endpoint localization cannot be made valid in the locked heat-kernel Wilson algebra.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote to proof delivery for this finite block if certified intervals prove M_G-alpha sum beta[D]_+-|T|>0 uniformly through cutoff removal.
control_decision.reason: This branch is not looping: it made a contribution-making post-H,K reduction from an indefinite endpoint cumulant to a clipped dominance certificate with a clear promotion/falsifier inequality.

dependency_updates.description: Compute G12(v), G13(v), G23(v) for every actual endpoint box in the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet three-hairpin regulator.
Use seven-point fourth-source stencils or an analytic heat-kernel expansion to bound beta_vD_v with M8 remainders.

Standard OS closed-cone and Wilson-loop renormalization arguments do not isolate the post-H,K Schur-Feshbach endpoint scalar or the half-dominance clipping [D_v]_+; this move is target-local to the finite hairpin handoff.
Surface source object, target object, same-theory condition, validity regimes, and non-claim boundaries for the endpoint clipping theorem.

falsifiers: A certified endpoint interval with eta_v<1/2 on enough beta_v mass and an upper bound making S_end<0 is a finite same-theory falsifier.
A valid source-stencil computation showing a negative nonlocal corner tail larger than M_G demotes the endpoint-box route.
If the straight f f contact fails to cancel after using the actual plaquette orientations, the clipped endpoint formula is invalid.
If Wilson loop renormalization at the reflection plane changes the endpoint source algebra, the same-theory bridge is falsified even if the regulated matrix stays positive.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: The endpoint contribution changes sign at eta_v=1/2. Symmetric endpoint boxes increase the margin, while sufficiently many pair-12-dominated boxes can overcome M_G and produce a determinant-level falsifier.
held_fixed_controls: Same heat-kernel regulator and gauge-invariant Wilson test algebra on source and target sides.
Fixed color normalization alpha_a=(g_a^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 and fixed post-H,K Gaussian margin M_G.
Fixed collar geometry away from endpoint redistribution, so PHP and the corrected second-order gate are unchanged.
No boundary counterterm, no altered Wilson loop renormalization, and no change of reflection plane.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch has already fixed H,K and reduced R to endpoint cumulants; another abstract restatement would loop. The concrete thought experiment tests the only remaining sign mechanism.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: Three reflected SU(N) Wilson hairpins in a heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulator, with the fixed Feshbach null vector and endpoint boxes partitioned into symmetric boxes and pair-12-dominated boxes.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: Certified source-derivative intervals for beta_vD_v, a uniform bound on endpoint/corner tails, and a cutoff-stable incidence table before the thought experiment can alter proof obligations.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: Endpoint dominance ratio eta_v=(G13(v)+G23(v))/G12(v), varied from eta_v=1 for symmetric endpoints to eta_v=0 for pure 12 endpoints.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 259 sharpens the remaining R problem: the negative compact-group endpoint kappa_4 is dangerous only after clipping by positive half-dominance D_v>0. Equal endpoint boxes are not merely harmless heuristically; they enter the protective part beta_v[-D_v]_+. The conceptual value signal is sharpness and route change: the proof state is now a finite interval problem for endpoint dominance and tails, not an abstract OS/Wilson obstruction ladder.

negative_tactic_decision.conflict_target: Same-theory OS positivity for the intended continuum Wilson Schwinger functions in this finite block.
negative_tactic_decision.contradiction_carrier_or_no_go_family: Finite three-hairpin Schur-Feshbach null-channel determinant after heat-kernel endpoint contraction.
escape_conditions: Endpoint dominance intervals satisfy eta_v>=1/2 or are too small to beat M_G.
Tail bound is sign-positive or uniformly below the remaining margin.
The endpoint source algebra is shown not to be dense in the same-theory Wilson core, demoting this to a regulator artifact.
negative_tactic_decision.exact_negation_or_method_class: Negate promotion by proving S_end<0 with certified source-derivative intervals for alpha sum beta[D]_+, protective safe terms, and tails.
negative_tactic_decision.next_validation_handoff: Produce a table of D_v signs, beta_v intervals, and tail intervals for the actual three-hairpin geometry.
negative_tactic_decision.paper_contribution_potential: A finite post-H,K endpoint certificate or counterexample would be a concrete appendix-level handoff beyond standard constructive-QFT OS positivity arguments.
proof_obligations: Compute the actual endpoint incidence table Gij(v).
Certify beta_v by heat-kernel source derivatives with uniform M8 bounds.
Bound nonlocal endpoint/corner tail T_a in the same regulator.
Show cutoff-removal stability of the clipped inequality.
negative_tactic_decision.reason_for_tactic: The fastest way to stress the same-theory bridge is to force eta_v<1/2 endpoint dominance and test whether the clipped negative cumulant beats M_G.

branch_outputs.next_experiment: Build the endpoint incidence table for the actual three-hairpin plaquette-sheet geometry, compute D_v=2G12-4G13-4G23 per endpoint box, and run the seven-point source stencil only on boxes with D_v>0 first.
